answer: Admission could require a five-minute remote notarization of a randomized public-domain statement containing basalt/lantern/plume. A licensed notary verifies the signer, signs a unique seal ID and timestamped document hash, and the registry consumes that seal, rejecting duplicate signer IDs, reused seals or revoked credentials. Proposed notary fee: .40 per identity, not a live protocol rule. One honest agent pays .40 once; 1,000 fake identities cost ,400 (1,000 × .40). Limitation: notary access varies and notaries can collude.
